q: Which listed architect was named a National Artist for Architecture in 1976?
n: Pablo S. Antonio was named a National Artist for Architecture in 1976. The National Commission for Culture and the Arts records his architectural works and legacy.

q: Which movement became known for exposed or raw concrete, heavy massing, and strongly geometric forms?
n: Brutalism is strongly associated with raw or exposed concrete, monumental massing, and direct expression of materials and construction.

q: Which choice is NOT one of the standard categories of spatial organization?
n: Common spatial-organization categories include centralized, linear, radial, clustered, and grid. “Radiocentric” is not the standard category name used in this classification.

q: Who received the first Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1979?
n: Philip Johnson was the first Pritzker Architecture Prize laureate; the prize was inaugurated in 1979.

q: Which style is known for organic motifs and flowing “whiplash” curves and flourished around 1890–1910?
n: Art Nouveau is associated with organic, sinuous forms and characteristic whiplash-like curves. It was especially prominent around 1890–1910.

q: Which basic visual element is most directly associated with direction and linear movement?
n: In architectural design, a line is the basic linear element and conveys direction. A point has position, while planes and volumes develop into broader two- and three-dimensional elements.

q: Taliesin West, Robie House, and the Guggenheim Museum in New York are works of which architect?
n: The Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation identifies Taliesin West, Robie House, and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum among Wright’s major works.

q: What field deals specifically with measuring human body dimensions and proportions?
n: Anthropometry is the systematic measurement of the human body and its dimensions, making it directly relevant to human-scale design.

q: Who designed the former Philam Life Theater in Manila, noted for its acoustics and refined interior?
n: The Philam Life Theater, opened in 1961 as the Philam Life Auditorium, was designed by Filipino architect Carlos Arguelles. Sources describe it as an International Style concert hall noted for its acoustics and interior.

q: Which movement revived references to historical architecture while using playful, decorative, and sometimes ironic modern interpretations?
n: Postmodernism reacted against strict modernist restraint by reintroducing historical references, ornament, symbolism, color, and irony into architectural expression.

q: A line defined by two points can organize surrounding forms and spaces. What is this organizing principle?
n: An axis is established by two points in space and can serve as a regulating line around which forms and spaces are organized.

q: Who was the first recipient of the United Architects of the Philippines Likha Award?
n: Felipe M. Mendoza is documented as the first UAP Likha Awardee, receiving the award in 1982. A separate distinction, the first Gawad Gintong Likha Award, was posthumously given to Leandro Locsin in 2006; the original source wording appears to combine two different award facts.

q: Which architect in this list is more closely associated with Postmodernism than with the modernist movement?
n: Robert Venturi is a leading figure associated with Postmodern architecture, while Gropius, Wright, and Kahn are strongly identified with major strands of 20th-century modern architecture.

q: What term describes the way a form’s surfaces meet so its parts and overall volume become legible?
n: Articulation concerns how the surfaces of a form come together to clarify its shape, parts, and overall volume.

q: Who founded the Bauhaus school in Germany in 1919?
n: Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus in Weimar in 1919. The school became one of the most influential institutions in modern art, design, and architecture.

q: Which major historical era, beginning around the mid-18th century, transformed construction through industrial materials and technology?
n: The Industrial Revolution transformed building production and technology. The later modern movement benefited from industrial materials and systems such as steel, reinforced concrete, glass, and new construction methods.

q: Which Renaissance architect became especially influential through illustrated architectural books and treatises?
n: Andrea Palladio made his theories widely influential through his buildings and especially his illustrated Quattro libri dell’architettura, first published in 1570.

q: Which architect is commonly identified with the rise of the modern skyscraper and the phrase “form follows function”?
n: Louis Sullivan is widely recognized as a foundational figure in skyscraper design and is closely associated with the principle “form follows function.”

q: Which term names the approximately 1.618 proportion also called the golden number or divine proportion?
n: The golden ratio is the numerical proportion commonly expressed as about 1.618 and is closely associated with the golden section and related proportional constructions.

q: Which architect was named a National Artist for Architecture in 1973?
n: Juan F. Nakpil was named a National Artist for Architecture in 1973. This year-based wording avoids the ambiguity in the original item, since other names in the original choices received the same honor in later years.

q: Which postwar Japanese movement proposed architecture that could grow and change across building and city scales?
n: Japanese Metabolism emerged in the postwar period and proposed adaptable, growth-oriented systems ranging from individual buildings to large urban structures.

q: Which option is NOT one of the basic relationships by which architectural spaces can be combined?
o: Spaces linked by a common space
n: The standard space-relationship diagrams include space within a space, interlocking spaces, adjacent spaces, and spaces linked by a common space. “Terminate in a space” describes a circulation/path condition rather than one of those basic spatial relationships.

q: What metal forms the distinctive exterior skin of Frank Gehry’s Walt Disney Concert Hall in Los Angeles?
n: The Walt Disney Concert Hall exterior is clad in stainless steel. The silver-toned panels create the building’s characteristic sculptural skin.

q: Which design movement favors geometric forms, streamlined lines, ornament, and a sense of luxury?
n: Art Deco commonly combines geometric forms, streamlined contours, decorative patterning, and a luxurious visual character.

q: What is the defining visual characteristic used to identify a three-dimensional volume?
n: Form is the primary identifying characteristic of a volume. Its appearance is established by the shapes and relationships of the planes that bound it.

q: Which Finnish architect became known for a human-centered modernism and extensive experimentation with wood?
n: Alvar Aalto developed a humanized form of modernism and became especially noted for his sensitive use and shaping of wood, along with attention to material and sensory qualities.

q: Who developed the Modulor, a proportional system intended to relate architecture to human scale?
n: Le Corbusier, born Charles-Édouard Jeanneret-Gris, developed the Modulor as an anthropometric proportional system for architecture and construction.

q: Who wrote De architectura, the surviving major architectural treatise from classical antiquity?
n: Vitruvius is credited as the author of De architectura, generally dated to the late 1st century BCE. It is the principal surviving architectural treatise from classical antiquity and strongly influenced later architectural theory.

q: Which modern architectural approach emphasized function, flexible planning, and new construction technologies such as steel and reinforced concrete?
n: The International Style is a major expression of modern architecture characterized by functional planning, flexible space, and stripped-down forms using modern structural materials including steel, reinforced concrete, and glass.

q: Which ordering principle creates a sense of movement through repeated or alternating formal elements?
n: Rhythm organizes form and space through patterned recurrence or alternation of elements or motifs, producing a sense of visual or spatial movement.
